title: 🗄️ How to Design an E-Commerce Database?
excerpt: How should we organize all this data? 🤔
body:
ㅤ
📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 06
ㅤ
Imagine building an e-commerce application where customers browse products, place orders, and make payments.

How should we organize all this data? 🤔

Storing everything in a single table might seem simple, but it can create duplicate data and make maintenance difficult.

That's where relational database design comes in!

Let's break it down. 👇
ㅤ
1️⃣ 𝗜𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗳𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗧𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀 📋

A basic e-commerce database might contain:

👤 Customers — Customer information
📦 Products — Product details and prices
🛒 Orders — Customer order information
🧾 Order_Items — Products included in each order
💳 Payments — Payment transaction details

Each table has a specific responsibility.
ㅤ
2️⃣ 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗣𝗿𝗶𝗺𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆𝘀 🔑

A Primary Key (PK) uniquely identifies each record in a table.

Example:

Customers
• customer_id (PK)
• name
• email

Products
• product_id (PK)
• name
• price

This helps us uniquely identify customers and products.
ㅤ
3️⃣ 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝗧𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗙𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗞𝗲𝘆𝘀 🔗

A Foreign Key (FK) creates a relationship between tables and helps maintain referential integrity.

Example:

Orders
• order_id (PK)
• customer_id (FK)
• order_date

Here, customer_id references the Customers table.

This allows each order to be linked to a customer.
ㅤ
4️⃣ 𝗛𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗹𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝘆-𝘁𝗼-𝗠𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀 🔄

One order can contain multiple products.

One product can appear in multiple orders.

We can solve this using an Order_Items table.

Order_Items
• order_item_id (PK)
• order_id (FK)
• product_id (FK)
• quantity
• unit_price

This connects Orders and Products without duplicating product details.
ㅤ
5️⃣ 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗧𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀 🧩

Here's how the tables connect:

✅ One Customer → Many Orders

✅ One Order → Many Order Items

✅ One Product → Many Order Items

✅ One Order → Multiple Payments (if supported)

These relationships help keep data organized and consistent.
ㅤ
6️⃣ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗗𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗚𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿? ⚙️

A well-designed relational database helps:

✅ Reduce unnecessary data duplication
✅ Maintain data integrity
✅ Simplify application maintenance
✅ Support efficient queries
✅ Make future development easier
ㅤ
💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

Good database design isn't just about creating tables.

It's about understanding how data is connected and organizing it to support real business requirements.

A strong database structure is an important foundation for building reliable and maintainable applications.
